item.title: China’s Xi greets Trump on arrival at Shenzhen airport
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping personally greeted Donald Trump at the airport as the US leader arrived Wednesday ahead of a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen that will also include Russia’s Vladimir Putin, AFP footage showed. After descending from Air Force One, Trump saluted as he stood alongside Xi on a red carpet lined with people waving colourful pom-poms and brandishing Chinese and American national flags, before the two leaders shook hands. Putin on war sanctions Meanwhile, President Vladimir Putin called Western sanctions on Russia a failure on Wednesday and met with his counterpart Xi Jinping in China ahead of their historic summit with US leader Donald Trump. Thursday’s trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could make decisions on the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence. Washington had signalled that Ukraine – something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem – was not expected to be addressed, before Trump said that it would. Putin, who met with Xi on Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen, was defiant on his war in Ukraine ahead of the three-man summit as he slammed Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion. “We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced an unprecedented sanctions pressure,” Putin said. After meeting the Russian leader, Xi urged closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should “leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties”. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said that sanctions on Russia “are going to continue to increase as long as this (Ukraine) war goes on.” Also up for discussion in Thursday’s trilateral meeting are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile Vanguard News The post China’s Xi greets Trump on arrival at Shenzhen airport appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK-based Nigerian pastor jailed nearly 12 years for rape
item.description: A Nigerian church leader based in the United Kingdom, Brein Ayeni, has been sentenced to 11 years and nine months in prison for repeatedly raping a woman and subjecting her to coercive and controlling behaviour. West Midlands Police disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying Ayeni, 43, was convicted of three counts of rape and one count of coercive or controlling behaviour following a trial. The offences were committed from June 2025, while Ayeni was head of Christworld Nation Church in Coventry, where he was regarded as a trusted figure in the community. The police said he recorded some of the attacks on his mobile phone and threatened to circulate the videos if the victim reported him, claiming they would show that the encounters were consensual. According to the statement, Ayeni also made derogatory remarks about the woman’s previous lifestyle and exhibited controlling behaviour after gaining her trust. The victim reported the abuse to the police in March 2026, prompting an investigation by specialist officers from the force’s Rape and Serious Sexual Offences team. Ayeni, who lived on Hurst Road, Coventry, was sentenced at Warwick Crown Court on Tuesday, November 10. In her victim impact statement, the woman said Ayeni’s position in the church had made her trust him, adding that the abuse had severely affected her mental and emotional well-being. “The title he held made me trust him, and that trust has been deeply damaged. The impact on my mental and emotional health is that I do not feel like the same person I was before all of this happened,” she said. She also described how the experience had affected her ability to trust others and maintain close relationships. “I struggle to trust people and allow them to get close to me because I am frightened of being taken advantage of again,” she said. The victim said reporting the abuse had required considerable courage because of the fear of being judged or disbelieved. Detective Sergeant Evie Griffiths, of the police force’s public protection unit, described the offences as horrific, noting that they had left the victim with lasting trauma. “These were horrific crimes which have understandably had a lasting impact. It is through her bravery in telling us what happened we were able to arrest Ayeni and stop him committing any further offences,” Griffiths said. She added that Ayeni had abused the trust placed in him to commit the offences and had been appropriately sentenced. The police also encouraged victims of rape and other sexual offences to seek support, whether or not they were ready to make a formal report. item.title: Putin says trilateral summit with Xi, Trump will be ‘very useful’
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Wednesday that he expected his trilateral summit with US and Chinese leaders Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to be “very useful”. “I expect the trilateral meeting between the Russian, Chinese, and American leaders, scheduled on the sidelines of the (APEC) summit, will be highly useful,” Putin said in Shenzhen, China a day before the first ever meeting between the three leaders. “In a contemporary world full of turbulence, amidst the fragmentation of the global economy, and at a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division, equality rather than hegemony, partnership rather than isolation, and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said. The Russian leader also said that Western sanctions imposed on Moscow since his 2022 invasion of Ukraine had “failed” and that Russia had come through “with dignity”. item.title: Five things to know about ‘Grand Theft Auto’
item.description: The video game that launched 1,000 controversies and made billions of dollars for its studio is back — “Grand Theft Auto VI” will hit a console near you on Thursday. It is widely expected to become the biggest game of the decade, with its launch coming 13 years after the previous edition scaled new heights in terms of gameplay and profitability. Here are five things to know about GTA: – Trailblazer – The first two games in the series, which debuted in 1997, offered a top-down view of the action as players took on the role of a criminal on missions around cities. But “GTA III” set the standard in 2001 for what games could be, offering a combination of a three-dimensional open world, advanced graphics and gameplay that won widespread critical acclaim and legions of fans. Each new GTA title since then has been hailed by both industry analysts and gamers for pushing the boundaries of the medium. – Cash cow – And they have all been bestsellers, bringing in billions of dollars for Take-Two Interactive, parent company of the Rockstar Games studio. Despite not releasing a flagship GTA game for more than a decade, the series has remained a cash cow, especially thanks to its multiplayer online version, where users can buy in-game items. The last game in the franchise, “GTA V”, was released in 2013 and reached $1 billion in retail sales “faster than any entertainment release in history”, Take-Two has said. “GTA V” has sold around 230 million copies, according to the company’s most recent figures, making it the second best-selling game of all time behind Minecraft. The entire GTA franchise has sold a mammoth 470 million units, according to Take-Two. – Magnet for controversy – With the wild success came a wave of controversies. Critics have accused the series of glorifying violence and encouraging players to engage in criminal behaviour — allegations Take-Two executives have denied. GTA games have also faced strong criticism for depictions of torture and misogynistic portrayals of women, many of whom appear as sex workers or strippers. It has also been accused of pushing ethnic caricatures — an AFP analysis found more than three-quarters of Italian and Russian characters were involved in criminal activity, compared with 27 percent of Americans. Despite being praised for their often biting cultural satire, the level of violence in the games has led to occasional bans and restrictions in some countries, including a chain of stores in Australia in 2014. – A cultural institution – GTA has become a cultural institution, spawning countless memes and attracting huge stars to its cast. Tommy Vercetti, the main character in 2002’s “GTA: Vice City”, was voiced by Hollywood star Ray Liotta. Other cameos in the series include Samuel L. Jackson, Burt Reynolds, musician Phil Collins and comedian Ricky Gervais. In 2021, hip-hop superstar Dr. Dre featured. item.title: Two Clocks, One Election
item.description: The government wants economic improvement to reach voters. The opposition wants negotiations to produce cooperation. Both are running against time. Two clocks are ticking towards Nigeria’s presidential election. One measures how quickly economic improvement becomes visible in people’s lives. The other measures how quickly opposition leaders can turn discussions into an arrangement that strengthens their challenge. This week has brought movement on both. Figures released on Monday put October’s annual headline inflation at 14.06 per cent, down from 14.63 per cent in September. Meanwhile, opposition parties have announced a November 23 summit in Abuja to adopt cooperation documents. These developments give the governing party and its challengers something concrete to discuss. Neither, by itself, settles the electoral argument. For President Bola Tinubu, the task is to demonstrate that reform is improving living standards. For the opposition, it is to demonstrate that cooperation can survive competing ambitions. Inflation Falls. The Household Test Remains. The latest inflation figures offer the government evidence for its argument that economic stabilisation is progressing. Food inflation also moderated, to 19.13 per cent year on year from 19.59 per cent. The political meaning requires care. A lower annual inflation rate means prices are rising more slowly than a year earlier. It does not mean that the general price level has returned to where it stood before the cost of living shock. Families judge affordability through income, food, transport, rent and other recurring expenses. A household can recognise an improving economic indicator while remaining under considerable pressure. The government therefore has an opening, accompanied by a demanding question: how much improvement will citizens experience before they vote? Its strongest argument would connect stabilisation with changes people can identify: more reliable services, stronger earnings, affordable essentials and business opportunities. The opposition also needs to respond seriously to improving data. It can question the distribution and adequacy of recovery while explaining how its own policies would improve purchasing power. The emerging debate should concern the route from economic stability to household security. November 23: Cooperation Acquires a Date The Coalition for Democracy says participating opposition parties will meet at the NAF Conference Centre in Abuja on Monday, November 23. The proposed business includes a National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, a Framework for Opposition Unity and a National Reform Programme. That is a clearer next step than another general declaration of willingness to work together. But several forms of cooperation remain possible. Parties can coordinate election monitoring, defend campaign freedoms and agree on institutional reforms while continuing to field competing presidential candidates. item.title: Avon Colour Run Takes Free Diabetes and Hypertension Checks to Over 1,000 Lagosians
item.description: On World Diabetes Day, more than 1,000 people at Eko Atlantic City, Lagos, did something many Nigerians put off for years: they checked their numbers. At the 2026 Avon Colour Run, organised by Avon Healthcare Limited (Avon HMO) and Avon Medical Practice, participants received free checks for noncommunicable diseases, including diabetes and hypertension, before and after a 5-kilometre run and walk. Diabetes and hypertension are among the conditions that often develop quietly. Many people live with them for years without symptoms, only to learn of them when complications set in. Holding the Colour Run on 14 November, the day set aside worldwide to raise awareness of diabetes, was a deliberate choice to bring that conversation to where people already were: out in the open, in motion and in good company. The Chief Executive Officer of Avon Medical Practice, Dr Akinbiyi Oke, said the aim was to make screening feel ordinary rather than frightening. “Most people do not avoid a health check because they do not care. They avoid it because it feels like bad news waiting to happen. When a blood sugar check sits next to a fitness session and a family picnic atmosphere, it becomes something you simply do. Knowing your numbers is the first step. What you do with them is the next, and our doctors and nurses are here to help with both.” Participants also took part in fitness sessions with Kemen and Mayorfit, a reminder that regular physical activity is one of the most accessible tools for lowering the risk of diabetes, hypertension and heart disease. The Chief Executive Officer of Avon HMO, Osa Imasogie, said prevention is also better for families’ finances and for the health system. “Treating advanced chronic disease is costly for families and for the whole system. Every condition caught early is a smaller bill, a shorter hospital stay and a longer, healthier life. A health plan gives you access to care but healthy habits give you fewer reasons to need it urgently. We want to help Nigerians build both.” As a practical takeaway, the organisers encouraged all Nigerians, whether or not they attended, to have their blood pressure and blood sugar checked at least once a year, and more often if there is a family history of diabetes or hypertension. The Colour Run was supported by Eko Atlantic City, UBA, Transcorp Plc, Heirs Technologies, Redtech, Heirs Energies, United Capital Group, Heirs Insurance Group and Aquafina. ### Media Enquiries Adeoye Falade Head, Brand, Marketing & Communications, Avon HMO Email: adeoye.falade@avonhealthcare.com Phone: 08057356974 The post Avon Colour Run Takes Free Diabetes and Hypertension Checks to Over 1,000 Lagosians appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Human’ is Cambridge Dictionary’s word of the year
item.description: “Human”, meaning to have the “qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines” has been named Cambridge Dictionary’s Word of the Year. In an era of rapidly expanding Artificial Intelligence (AI) and dire warnings it could even wipe out humanity, the word captured “the 2026 zeitgeist”, Cambridge University Press board member Francesca Woodward told AFP. Over the past 12 months, she said, people had been “really considering what it is to be human” in particular due to concerns about AI taking over their jobs. “I think people are trying to remind themselves of … what human means,” she said. The word beat off competition from other words related to AI and the online world, reflecting intense global interest in how technology is changing our lives, she said. The dictionary’s lexicographers had also observed an increased used of “human” in compound words such as human-made or human author, she added. Tom McClelland, a philosopher of science at the University of Cambridge, described “human” as a “really interesting choice … because right now our understanding of humanity is changing”. – Global AI debate – “We’re trying to understand the difference between a human mind and an artificial mind, between living beings like us and artificial beings that we’re creating. What sets us apart, is it consciousness, creativity or compassion?” he said. The focus on what it means to be human has seen global leaders and prominent figures such as Pope Leo XIV, Bill Gates, classicist Mary Beard and actor Cate Blanchett weigh in on the debate. Other contenders for the word of the year crown included “agent, meaning an artificial intelligence system that can operate in a complicated way without human control. Also in the running was “wholesome”, defined as “good for you, and likely to improve your life either physically, morally, or emotionally”. “Dusking” was also in contention, the practice of watching daylight turn to darkness as a form of relaxation. A Dutch tradition, it has been revived as a way of reconnecting with the natural world. Other new words added to the dictionary in 2026 included “aura farming”, doing things to show a personality that people will admire, and “looksmaxing”, making yourself as physically attractive as possible. The word of the year and new additions are selected using a range of criteria including the words searched for on the Cambridge Dictionary website. Among words to watch for next year, according to Cambridge Dictionary, were FOBO, “fear of becoming obsolete” because your job can be performed by AI. Another was “weather whiplash”, denoting a “quick change from one extreme of weather to another”. Last year’s word of the year was “parasocial” to describe the sense of having a connection to a famous person you do not know personally or a fictional character. item.title: Paz At The Double As Argentina Thrash Costa Rica
item.description: Rising star Nico Paz scored a superb double as Argentina bounced back from defeat with a 7-0 thrashing of Costa Rica in a friendly on Tuesday. Italy-based Como attacking midfielder Paz — who has emerged as a reported transfer target for incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino — underscored his talent with two spectacular first-half goals in Cordoba. The 22-year-old, who scored twice in Como’s 4-1 Champions League drubbing of United last month, lashed in Argentina’s opener after just eight minutes at the Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium. After Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez doubled Argentina’s lead in the 35th minute, Paz then grabbed his second with the goal of the game. Picking up the ball in midfield, the young forward held off the attention of several Costa Rican markers before twisting and turning into space inside the penalty area and crashing a shot into the top corner to make it 3-0. Alvarez put Argentina into a 4-0 lead in the 43rd minute, beating Costa Rica goalkeeper Patrick Sequeira at the near post with a vicious shot that flew into the roof of the net. Paz’s virtuoso first-half performance was the highlight of a one-sided encounter as Argentina bounced back from suffering a 2-1 defeat to Uruguay in Buenos Aires on Friday. Argentina’s midfielder #07 Giuliano Simeone and Costa Rica’s forward #07 John Paul Ruiz fight for the ball during the international friendly football match between Argentina and Costa Rica at Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium in Cordoba, Argentina on November 17, 2026. (Photo by Diego Lima / AFP) | Diego Lima / AFP Paz was substituted at half-time by Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni for Franco Mastantuono, the 19-year-old Fiorentina forward. Like Paz, Mastantuono is another member of Argentina’s next generation of young talent as the former world champions rebuild following the retirement from international football of Lionel Messi. Mastantuono was quick to make his own mark on Tuesday’s friendly, scoring just three minutes after coming on at half-time to make it 5-0. Liverpool’s Alexis Mac Allister swept in a sixth goal in the 78th minute before Mastantuono grabbed his second of the night two minutes from time with a thumping low strike. item.title: Gulf Nations Attacked After US Strikes Iranian Island
item.description: Bahrain and Kuwait said Wednesday that they had repelled air attacks launched against them following US strikes on an Iranian island, as Gulf nations face retaliatory bombardment in the Middle East war. The conflict — which began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February — has spilled over to Gulf states that host US military facilities. The Iranian army said Wednesday its drones “targeted Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms belonging to the terrorist US military at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait,” in a statement carried by state television IRIB. Kuwait’s military said Wednesday its air defences were “responding to hostile drone threats”, urging its public to follow security and safety advice. While Bahrain said its air defences intercepted attacks from Iran early Wednesday, a day after Tehran’s Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a base used by Washington. Iranians wave flags during a gathering in front of an anti-US billboard depicting US President Donald Trump in Tehran’s Enghelab Square on November 3, 2026. Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP The United States and Iran are in a standoff over the vital Strait of Hormuz, with the US military working to escort ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Tehran’s attempts to close the waterway. Iran’s official IRNA news agency cited a regional official as saying the United States had hit Qeshm Island in the Hormuz Strait without causing serious damage. US fighter jets “used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island”, an American official told AFP on condition of anonymity, adding that the strike was in response to Iranian “aggression targeting US personnel and assets”. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said on Wednesday it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the Iran-backed group toward the Riyadh area. Mourners carry the bodies of members of Iraq’s Hashed al-Shaabi, or Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), a paramilitary alliance that includes pro-Iran groups, who were killed earlier in Diyala in central Iraq by US-Saudi strikes, during the funeral in Baghdad on July 29, 2026. (Photo by Murtadha Ridha / AFP) / Alleged Iran Plot Explosions boomed across Bahrain’s capital on Tuesday as a mobile phone alert warned residents to seek safety. Bahrain’s armed forces said they “confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today… before they could achieve their objectives”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US-operated radar system. “Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain,” the Guards’ Sepah news website said. item.title: Barau, Atiku, others mourn late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: By Henry Umoru & Olasunkanmi Akoni ABUJA—THE presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar; Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin (APC, Kano North) has mourned the passing of Mr. Olufemi Ajasa, the Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers. Also, Chairman of Ikeja Local Government Area, Lagos, Akeem Dauda, mourned the death of Mr. Ajasa, describing his passing as a painful loss to the media industry and the journalism profession. Ajasa passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, after a brief illness at the age of 44, according to the management of Vanguard Media Limited, publishers of the Vanguard Newspapers. Ajasa’s death painful loss to journalism, Vanguard — Atiku mourns Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s Online Editor, Olufemi Ajasa, as a painful loss to the journalism profession and the media organisation, extending his condolences to the management, staff and family of the deceased. Atiku, in a condolence message on his X handle on Tuesday, expressed sadness over Ajasa’s death at the age of 44, saying his passing was a reminder of how suddenly a life devoted to work, family and service could be cut short. He wrote: “Ajasa’s passing is a deep loss to @vanguardngrnews and to the journalism profession. Behind every story published and every deadline met is a commitment to keeping the public informed. “His colleagues have lost a valued teammate, the media community a respected professional, and his family a beloved son, husband, father and brother.” Atiku also extended his condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the newspaper’s Editor, Eze Anaba, and everyone who knew and worked with the late journalist. “I extend my heartfelt condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, Editor Eze Anaba, and all who loved and worked with him,” the statement added. Memories “May the memories they shared bring comfort in this difficult hour, and may God grant his family strength to bear this immeasurable loss”, he wrote. In a condolence message by his spokesperson, Ismail Mudashir, Senator Barau described the late Ajasa as a thoroughbred professional and one of the finest minds in Nigeria’s digital journalism space. He said: “Femi Ajasa’s dedication and commitment to truth and accuracy set him apart and distinguished him among others. His death is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family, the Vanguard family, but to the entire Nigerian media industry.” He noted that Mr. Ajasa’s journalism journey, which began as a photojournalist with the National Mirror in 2012, through TheNewsGuru and Pulse, to his return to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, was marked by excellence, integrity and selfless service to the country through his noble profession, journalism. item.title: Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom
item.description: US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations. Huang sought to be reinstated despite resigning last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but his successor — interim CEO Colette Kress — said that it was now “business as usual” at the company as it charts a way ahead without him. Harvey Jones, the chair of the company’s board, said in an earnings call that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies. “Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in her first remarks since being appointed by the board last week. She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 percent in next fiscal year, up from 70 percent. Huang’s bid on Tuesday to get his job back was the latest twist for the company at the center of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth. The recent upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia — which has lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke — and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns. A charismatic promoter of AI, his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations. – Battle over AI chips – “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said, hours before the earnings release. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” As the spy scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing. The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Under Washington’s new rules, data centers anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes. item.title: Kwara APC Reps candidate unveils people-centred agenda
item.description: …Says serving as AbdulRazaq’s CPS was greatest privilege By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin ILORIN — The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives election, Dr Rafiu Ajakaye, has unveiled a legislative agenda focusing on security, education, youth employment, women’s economic empowerment and rural development. Ajakaye, a former Chief Press Secretary to Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, said his aspiration to represent the constituency was driven by a desire to provide accessible and effective leadership rather than pursue personal ambition. He stated this on Tuesday while speaking on the News Keg programme organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) at its secretariat in Ilorin. Presenting his manifesto titled, “Manifesto of Purpose: A Covenant with the People of Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency”, Ajakaye described his service as the governor’s spokesperson as a major privilege in his professional career. “Serving as the Chief Press Secretary to Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq was one of the greatest privileges of my life,” he said. He described public office as a responsibility that should be directed towards improving people’s lives. Ajakaye cited his involvement in the 2021, 2024 and 2025 teachers’ recruitment exercises under the AbdulRazaq administration as an experience that reinforced his belief in merit-based employment opportunities. According to him, the exercises demonstrated the importance of involving the right people in recruitment processes to ensure fairness and create opportunities for qualified applicants. “Leadership is not about occupying an office. It is about inspiring hope, solving problems, expanding opportunities, and shaping a future in which every citizen can live with dignity,” he said. The candidate, who hails from Alabe community in Ifelodun Local Government Area, said his background, academic training and professional experience had shaped his approach to governance and public service. He said his experience as a journalist, public relations practitioner and public servant, particularly his years as the governor’s spokesperson, had exposed him to policymaking and the importance of transparency, competence and integrity in governance. On security, Ajakaye identified banditry and kidnapping as major concerns affecting rural communities, saying the activities had disrupted livelihoods and economic activities. He pledged to advocate stronger legislative oversight of security agencies, improved welfare and equipment for security personnel, intelligence-led operations and community-based security strategies. He identified insecurity in parts of Ifelodun Local Government Area as a major priority, promising to make it the foremost issue on his legislative agenda if elected. “Security is number one on my legislative agenda. item.title: Matawalle’s support group targets release of 2,000 inmates
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The Tinubu Again Movement (TAM), a political support group associated with the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has announced plans to facilitate the release of 2,000 inmates in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states through the payment of court-imposed fines and other lawful interventions. The proposed initiative is aimed at assisting indigent inmates whose continued detention is linked to their inability to pay fines and those eligible for release under applicable laws. The group announced the plan on Tuesday during its participation in the presidential campaign rally of President Bola Tinubu in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State. Hundreds of its members participated in the rally, wearing branded outfits and carrying banners bearing the images of Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and Matawalle. The supporters also marched through major streets of the state capital, expressing support for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. Speaking on the proposed intervention, TAM spokesman, Mallam Yusuf Dingyadi, said the initiative was designed to assist deserving inmates who could not secure their release because of financial constraints. He said the movement would identify eligible beneficiaries and work towards settling outstanding fines in accordance with the law. “Our intention is to facilitate the release of 2,000 inmates across Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states by identifying deserving cases and assisting those whose continued detention is linked to their inability to pay relatively small fines. “We believe that imprisonment should not become a permanent barrier to rebuilding one’s life, particularly for individuals who qualify for release under the law but remain in correctional facilities because of their financial circumstances,” Dingyadi said. He added that the intervention was intended to support family reunification and the reintegration of eligible former inmates into society. Dingyadi also disclosed that the movement was planning humanitarian interventions for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable communities across the three states. According to him, the proposed programmes would include the distribution of food, clothing and other essential relief materials, as well as empowerment initiatives. “We are equally concerned about the humanitarian challenges confronting internally displaced persons in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states. We intend to support them through the provision of foodstuffs, clothing and empowerment opportunities to cushion their hardships and restore their dignity,” he said. item.title: Immigration vows to fix gaps in Visa & Residency Reforms
item.description: .As Army pledges stronger partnership on border security By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Nigeria Immigration Service NIS on Tuesday undertook a stakeholders’ assessment of its Visa and Residency Reforms, one year after the scheme was rolled out, promising to confront all the weak points. Comptroller General of the NIS, Kemi Nandap, made the pledge in Abuja, while declaring open a one-day stakeholders’ sensitization workshop on the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms. At the event, the Nigerian Army also pledged a stronger partnership with the Service in securing the country’s borders, especially in areas where a large portion of the frontier remains porous. The Chief of Civil-Military Affairs (Army), Major General Musa Etsu-Ndagi, who represented the Chief of Army Staff COAS, said: “Nigeria has a land border of 4,047km and there is a large portion of it that remains porous. The Nigerian Army will continue to support the NIS in manning the borders especially in those areas”. On the reforms, the CGIS who was represented by the Deputy Comptroller General DCG in charge of Visa and Residency, Dr Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, said; “As we assess the implementation of the reforms over the last one year, we have reasons to appreciate the progress made so far. However, we must also be ready to identify the areas where we have not done well and take the necessary steps to address them”. The workshop was held under the theme: “Assessing the Implementation of the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms: Stakeholders’ Engagement and Strategies for Improved Service Delivery.” Nandap said the purpose of the meeting was to look at the progress made since the introduction of the reforms, discuss the challenges encountered and identify areas where improvements are needed.” She acknowledged that users may have run into difficulties since the introduction of these reforms. “These may include payment difficulties, technical issues and other concerns relating to the use of the portal. I want to assure you that the Service is willing to listen to your concerns and consider useful recommendations that will help us improve our operations,” she said. According to her, the reforms were introduced “to address some of the challenges associated with the old manual processes, reduce delays, improve transparency, strengthen national security and make our immigration services more accessible to the public.” Nandap listed the electronic visa (e-Visa) among the major gains, noting that it became operational on 1st May, 2025, and replaced the traditional Visa-on-Arrival arrangement. “Applicants can now receive decisions on their visa applications within 48 hours, subject to meeting the necessary requirements and security checks,” she said. She added that the e-Visa had “improved transparency, reduced unnecessary human interference and strengthened our ability to monitor visa applications and approvals.” The Comptroller General also cited the creation of the F9A and F9B visa categories for adult an

item.title: FMCGs seek NAFDAC automation to cut registration delays, fake licences
item.description: By Cynthia Alo Fast-Moving Consumer Goods, FMCG, manufacturers and small businesses have urged the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, to automate most of its paper processes involving product registration and licence renewal to reduce delays and curb circulation of counterfeit products and fake registration numbers. They said prolonged approvals were forcing some manufacturers to rely on intermediaries, exposing them to exploitation, including the use of fake NAFDAC registration numbers. The call was made recently at the 2026 FMCG Festival in Lagos. Speaking on behalf of manufacturers, Project Director of the FMCG Festival, Flora Mbeledeogu, said renewal of NAFDAC licences remained a major challenge, and that NAFDAC needed more hands and automation to make registration and renewal faster and more seamless. Mbeledeogu said: “We need NAFDAC to employ more hands and automate our systems so that when a consumer brand wants to renew its NAFDAC certificate or licence, they can do so without having to raise an arm and a leg. It has to just be a seamless process, just like it is in other countries in Africa where you just need to upload the required documents on the portal; within 24 hours, receive notification for factory inspection; officials inspect and take samples; analysis is done;by 48 hours, the product registration number is issued. We need to get to that point.” She warned that delays could expose smaller manufacturers to exploitation by intermediaries who claim to facilitate registration and renewal processes. She urged the agency to address the bottlenecks before the next edition of the festival. Responding to the concerns, Director, NAFDAC, North-West Zone, Dadi Mullah, said the agency’s processes were designed to ensure products met required health and safety standards. He disclosed that food product registration could take up to 120 working days, covering facility inspection, laboratory testing, regulatory assessment and final approval. Mullah said one challenge was that some small businesses wanted to produce from their domestic kitchens without meeting the facility requirements prescribed for commercial production. He said NAFDAC could not allow such businesses to supply the wider market without complying with Good Manufacturing Practices, GMP. He said: “The only thing I know that many of you will complain about is our facility requirement. We insist that unless the facility meets minimum good manufacturing practices requirements, we will not allow you to produce.Your kitchen cannot produce the kind of products for the international market.” Speaking on delays in registration and renewal processing, he said NAFDAC’s laboratories handled a large volume of applications, making it difficult for applicants to expect immediate results. item.title: Abia making steady progress under my watch — Otti
item.description: Pledges support for emerging talents to attain global recognition By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has said the state is making steady progress, expressing optimism about its development prospects under his administration. Otti spoke at the grand finale of the 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Talent Show 2026 in Umuahia, where he highlighted his administration’s efforts to reposition the state’s economy and promote development across various sectors. The governor, who was represented by his Chief of Staff, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, also pledged government support for the discovery, development and international promotion of indigenous talents. He said the administration was committed to creating opportunities for gifted young people to develop their abilities and gain recognition beyond Nigeria. Reflecting on the state’s development journey, Otti said his administration had prioritised efforts to harness Abia’s economic and human resources. “Before Otti came on board, Abia was lying fallow and prostrate. Nothing good was being said of Abia State. Today, Abia is being celebrated as a place of excellence,” he said. The governor said purposeful leadership and collaboration were important in unlocking the state’s human and creative potential. He assured participants in the talent show that the government would support successful contestants in pursuing opportunities for international recognition. Otti also disclosed that the state government would partner with Vision Africa International to advance the initiative. “Everybody that emerges here today is going global. His Excellency is going to make sure that global stardom is achieved,” he said. He described the talent show as consistent with his administration’s commitment to identifying, nurturing and promoting the abilities of young people. Earlier, the Chairman of the occasion, Noah Dallaji, represented by Theo Ubani, said Africa’s human talent remained one of the continent’s major competitive advantages. “I tell people that Africa has talent to offer. We might not offer the best in technology, but what we can offer is talent,” he said. In his welcome address, the founder and President of Vision Africa International, Archbishop Sunday Onuoha, called on political leaders to create conditions that would enable disadvantaged citizens to benefit from peace and development. Onuoha, who is also Co-Chairman of the Interfaith Dialogue Forum for Peace, said Nigeria’s diversity should promote unity rather than division. He urged Nigerians to work together across their differences to build a peaceful and prosperous country. The 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Talent Show was held under the theme, “The Sound of Peace: Breaking Barriers, Building Bridges.” The post Abia making steady progress under my watch — Otti appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Itsekiri youths suspend campaign rally boycott after governor’s intervention
item.description: Itsekiri apex youth bodies, Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths, UIY, and Itsekiri National Youth Council, INYC, have reiterated their opposition to the inclusion of the Ijaw in the Warri South ward delineation. They expressed surprise at the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s, decision to upload wards with names that have no historical, geographical or traditional relationship with Warri South, saying the move could trigger serious crises. They, however, decided to temporarily suspend mass action against all forms of political activities in Warri Kingdom following the intervention of Governor Sheriff Oborevwori. The INYC President, Appearance Efejuku, and UIY President, Joseph Okotie, made this known in a statement. The statement read: “Sequel to the memorandum of threat issued to the general public over the readiness of the Itsekiri apex youth bodies, UIY and INYC, to prevent the hosting of all forms of campaign rallies in any part of Warri Kingdom until all issues associated with the illegal creation of wards for the Ijaws are addressed satisfactorily, the Governor of Delta State, Right Honorable Elder Francis O. Oborevwori, invited us, leaders and other stakeholders, for a closed-door meeting, wherein he requested to know why the issuers of the threats took such a position. According to him, as of the last time he checked, the entire Itsekiri nation endorsed him and Mr. President. Thus, if this issue raised in the memo is not addressed, it could be misconstrued as a change in the position of the Itsekiri nation against the APC as a political party. “In response, the leadership of the two youth bodies was very categorical in their vehement opposition to any inclusion of Ijaws by any consideration into Warri South ward delineation. “As this would amount to disrespecting the directive of the President (His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu), who asked the Itsekiris and the Urhobos of Warri South to go and meet, sort out the issues, and get back to him. They also said that the President further stated that if the parties involved in these delineation issues were not satisfied, he would have no other option than to take the Supreme Court judgment back to the Supreme Court for proper interpretation. “They were therefore surprised to wake up one day and be told, in flagrant disregard of this directive of the President, that INEC had uploaded wards with names that have no historical, geographical or traditional relationship with Warri South. “This, according to the bodies, is a recipe for serious crises if INEC is not made to retrace its steps. “Thereafter, the Governor appealed to the leadership of the youth bodies to sheath their swords so he could take this issue back to the President for better clarification. “Additionally, it was stated that the only ward structure that was operational before now was the 12-ward structure, and it is what will be used to conduct the 2027 general election. “Consequent upon all that was mentioned, the leadership of

item.title: Nigeria, others lose $125bn yearly to illicit financial flows, $80bn to corruption — AU anti-graft body
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Folarin Kehinde ABUJA – Nigeria and other countries across Africa lose an estimated $125 billion annually to illicit financial flows and another $80 billion to corruption, with the losses potentially representing 50 per cent of the continent’s domestic revenue mobilisation and 25 per cent of its Gross Domestic Product (GDP), African Union’s anti-graft body has said. The staggering losses show how corruption and illicit financial transactions are draining resources that could otherwise finance development, strengthen public institutions and improve the lives of millions of Africans. The African Union is now seeking stronger asset recovery mechanisms and international cooperation to reverse the trend. Chairman of the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption (AUABC), Hon. Kwami Senanu, disclosed the figures at the First General Assembly of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners’ Forum (AARP-F) in Abuja, calling for urgent action to ensure that stolen wealth is recovered and put to productive use. Senanu said estimates by the AU’s United Nations partners put annual losses to corruption at about $80 billion, while other stakeholders on the continent estimated that illicit financial flows cost Africa approximately $125 billion yearly. “It is a fact that Africa continues to lose vast amounts of resources every year to corruption and illicit financial flows. Our UN partners put in about $80 billion annually. “Some other stakeholders on the continent look at about $125 billion being lost annually just to illicit financial flows. Approximately, perhaps about 50% of our domestic revenue mobilization and 25% of GDP is being lost, this is a very important issue,” he said. He urged African countries to move beyond declarations and commitments to concrete action, insisting that recovered assets must be returned, retained and managed in ways that directly benefit citizens. “Beyond our convictions and commitments, let us leave Abuja with plans and sustained actions that ensure that under CAPAR, under this Forum and under this General Assembly, we will have assets recovered, we will have assets retained, and assets managed in ways that absolutely benefit our continent,” Senanu said. Also speaking, Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Dr Musa Adamu Aliyu, SAN, said the increasingly sophisticated and transnational nature of corruption had made asset recovery more difficult, with stolen wealth concealed, transferred or invested across multiple jurisdictions through complex financial arrangements designed to frustrate investigations. Aliyu, who also chairs the Interim Steering Council of AARP-F, said no country or institution could effectively confront the challenge in isolation, stressing the need for mutual trust, sustained cooperation, timely information exchange, specialised expertise and collaboration across legal and institutional boundaries. item.title: Kano Govt pledges ₦100m, donates bus to Legal Aid Council
item.description: The Kano State Government has pledged ₦100 million and a brand-new operational bus to the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria to strengthen the delivery of free legal services to indigent and vulnerable citizens. Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf announced the support when he received the Chairman of the Governing Board of the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria, Justice Sulaiman Durosinlorun Kawu, alongside the Director-General, management team and other officials of the Council during a courtesy visit to the Government House, Kano. The governor said poverty should not deprive anyone of access to justice, stressing that no indigent or vulnerable citizen should remain in detention without legal representation simply because of a lack of financial resources. He commended the Council for its contributions to the administration of justice, particularly its provision of free legal representation and assistance to Nigerians who cannot afford the services of private legal practitioners. Yusuf reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to strengthening its partnership with the Council, promising necessary logistical, administrative and financial support within available resources. As part of efforts to improve the Council’s operations in the state, the governor directed the commissioners for Justice and Works to assess its office facilities for possible renovation and upgrading. He also ordered improvements in office furniture and electricity supply to provide a more conducive working environment. In addition to the ₦100 million pledged to the Council’s national headquarters, Yusuf assured its Kano State office of continued financial assistance and promised a new bus to facilitate its operations and outreach activities across the state. The governor urged government institutions, particularly agencies in the justice sector, to cooperate with the Council to enable it to discharge its responsibilities effectively. He also called on Nigerians to sustain peaceful coexistence, support national development and pray for the country’s leaders, while urging collective commitment to ensuring free, fair and peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections. Earlier, Kawu commended the governor for his commitment to the welfare and development of Kano State. He explained that the Council’s visit was part of its working tour of the North-West geopolitical zone, aimed at strengthening partnerships with state governments, assessing the delivery of legal aid services and promoting wider access to justice. Kawu disclosed that the Council provided legal assistance to approximately 2,500 people in Kano State between 2021 and 2023. He added that the Council had also facilitated the release of about 20 inmates by paying fines and court-ordered compensation on behalf of individuals who could not afford the payments. item.title: Nigeria is US’s greatest ally in Africa — American strategist says, as Tinubu grants interview to London
item.description: An American political strategist, Diana London, has described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, citing the growing security partnership between the two countries under Presidents Donald Trump and Bola Tinubu. London made the assertion in a post on her X handle on Wednesday, praising the cooperation between the Trump and Tinubu administrations in tackling terrorism and strengthening bilateral relations. She said the security partnership was producing results and could open up wider economic and trade opportunities for both countries. “The U.S.-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace Through Strength “None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government. “Because of the success of their partnership and relationship, the economic and trade opportunities are endless. The best is yet to come. Nigeria is the United States’ greatest ally in Africa,” she wrote. In another post, London expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria and promoting relations between the Nigerian government and the Trump administration. She said, “It has been an honour to work on the team of people representing Nigeria and helping to protect religious groups and further the relationship between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government.” Meanwhile, President Tinubu has granted an exclusive interview to London, an American political strategist and media personality. The development was disclosed by Imran Muhammad, Senior Special Assistant on New Media to the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, in a post on his X handle. Muhammad said the interview was expected to be released soon. “President Tinubu has held an exclusive interview with Dianna London, a prominent American media personality. The interview is anticipated to be released soon,” he wrote. The interview is expected to provide further insight into the Tinubu administration’s engagement with the United States, particularly on security cooperation and bilateral relations.
